No. - 8734 of 2023 Applicant :- Sunil Kumar Opposite Party :- State Of U.P. And Another Counsel for Applicant :- Ashok Gupta,Akash Kishan Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A. Hon'ble Shekhar Kumar Yadav,J. 1. 2. This anticipatory bail application (under section 438 Cr.P.C.) has been moved seeking bail in Case Crime No. 122 of 2023, under Sections 420, 467, 468, 471, 272, 273 I.P.C., Section 59 of Food Safety & Standards Act, 2006, Section 63, 65, 68 of Copyright Act, 1957 & Sections 103, 104 of Trademark Act, 1999, P.S.- Kotwali Rajapur, District- Chitrakoot.
texts.facts: 2. This anticipatory bail application (under section 438 Cr.P.C.) has been moved seeking bail in Case Crime No. 122 of 2023, under Sections 420, 467, 468, 471, 272, 273 I.P.C., Section 59 of Food Safety & Standards Act, 2006, Section 63, 65, 68 of Copyright Act, 1957 & Sections 103, 104 of Trademark Act, 1999, P.S.- Kotwali Rajapur, District- Chitrakoot.
texts.arguments: 3. Learned counsel for the applicant submitted that the applicant has been falsely implicated in the present case due to ulterior motive. He submitted that applicant is neither the owner of the concerned factory nor any incriminating article has been recovered from the possession of the Sunil Kumar vs State Of U.P. And Another on 3 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/62093827/ 1 applicant. He further submitted that the premises from where raid is alleged to have been made, does not belong to the applicant. He submitted that applicant has no concern with the alleged recovery, which was done from the possession of co-accused persons, namely, Jugraj Kesarwani and Dev Kumar Yadav and they have already granted regular bail by the court below. He further submitted that procedure of Trademark Act, 1999 have also not been followed. He submitted that investigation is still going on and no charge-sheet has been till date. The applicant is having no previous criminal history as has been mentioned in paragraph 28 of the affidavit. Learned counsel for the applicant further submits that applicant has apprehension of imminent arrest and in case, applicant is released on anticipatory bail, he will not misuse the liberty and would co-operate with the trial. 4. Learned A.G.A. has opposed the prayer for anticipatory bail of the applicant. He has submitted that in view of the seriousness of the allegations made against the applicant, he is not entitled to grant of anticipatory bail. The apprehension of the applicant is not founded on any material on record. Only on the basis of imaginary fear, anticipatory bail cannot be granted. 5. Hence without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case and considering the nature of accusations and antecedents of applicant, he is directed to be enlarged on anticipatory bail as per the Constitution Bench judgment of the Apex Court in the case of Sushila Aggarwal vs. State (NCT of Delhi)- 2020 SCC Online SC 98. (ii) The applicant shall not, directly or indirectly, make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer.
